title: Affine mate calculation for the fixed tensor model
statement: Let R,A,R',A' be commutative rings with R-algebra structures on A,R' and a structure map A tensor_R R' to A'. Let phi_g':A to A' and phi_f':R' to A' be its restrictions and assume their spectrum square is cartesian. Let M be an A-K-flat unbounded complex, K a quasi-coherent derived object on Spec A, e:Q(tilde M) isomorphic to K, L=Lg'^*K quasi-coherent and its counit on tilde M invertible. For the fixed library tensor model m=ModuleCat.baseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel R A R' M A' and any integer i, use the explicit U and a of [def-pc-affine-base-change-tilde-coordinates] with canonical target coordinate b. There exist a natural affine direct-image cohomology presentation d:Gamma H^i(-), restricted to R' and associated sheaf, isomorphic to H^i(Rf'_*(-)), and eU:tilde(restrict_R' U) isomorphic to H^i(Lg^*Rf_*K), with eU.hom followed by cohomology of the canonical base-change mate equal to tilde(restrict_R' a) followed by d at L. No stalk or localization conclusion is asserted. The universal comparison between arbitrary tensor models is not part of this fixed-model calculation.

source.place: Independence of choices for derived change of rings; affine base-change cohomology calculation

proof.text: For the library's fixed model, use the R-K-flat scalar-extension construction and exact tilde to identify the source cohomology. Transport along the cartesian tensor-algebra isomorphism to A'. Unlike the parent, no comparison of arbitrary universal models is needed here.

Affine higher-direct-image vanishing supplies hacyc in the natural unbounded derived pushforward cohomology theorem. Compose that natural isomorphism with the tilde/Gamma counit on quasi-coherent cohomology and the natural pushforward/restriction-of-scalars section comparison. This constructs d naturally on the whole quasi-coherent derived category, not merely at L.

On the common K-flat span the tensor-pullback unit equation identifies the scheme derived mate with the ring comparison. Use m.comparison_eq and m.localized_eq to identify its D-extension with the prescribed a. The target coordinate b uses the same inverse counit and e. Apply homology to obtain the global square.
